title: Level 5 (World Class) - B-22
notes:
West leads the ♠10 against 6NT. The opening spade lead is won in dummy. West's heart preempt has marked him with all 7 outstanding hearts and East with the ♦A. If West has the ♦Q, South should be able to succeed.

A diamond is played from North. If East wins the ♦A, West eventually will be subjected to a simple squeeze. East must, therefore, duck and South wins the ♦K. The spades and clubs are cashed. On the last club, West must pitch a diamond coming down to a singleton ♦Q. South exits a diamond.

If East plays low, West is left on lead and endplayed. If East overtakes, he establishes a diamond trick in dummy. East, with only diamonds left, must allow South to reach this stranded winner.

This ending is called a winkle. A winkle is a 2-loser squeeze that forces the defense to block a suit. Declarer can take advantage of the blockage by exiting that suit, forcing either the lead into a tenace or the building of a winner in the blocked suit.
